title: Tranche source seal + independent clean-worktree replay
deliberately_excluded: pre-existing uncommitted work from other in-progress fleets (CLI mining bridges, .claude/settings.json, mining.rs, oc_petri_net.rs, breeds/frame.rs, Cargo.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, CLAUDE.md) — left untouched per CLAUDE.md's multi-agent warning, not bundled into this seal
method: EnterWorktree, then git checkout <seal_commit> directly (the default worktree base branched from origin/main, the wrong ref — corrected by checking out the exact sealed SHA). All commands below ran in that isolated, clean worktree — a separate process, separate filesystem state, independent of the original session that produced the receipts being verified.

positive_witness_results.result: REPRODUCED WITH A NEW FINDING: full parallel `cargo test --lib` (default) showed 1 flaky failure — cache::tests::test_columnar_cache_roundtrip, panic 'should be cached' at cache.rs:469. Re-ran cache:: tests alone with --test-threads=1: 18/18 pass. Root cause identified: cache_clear() (cache.rs:177-184) unconditionally clears the entire process-global COLUMNAR_CACHE, not scoped to any test's own keys — test_cache_clear and test_columnar_cache_roundtrip share that global Mutex<FxHashMap>, and under cargo test's default parallel execution, test_cache_clear's clear() can race between test_columnar_cache_roundtrip's insert and its read-back. This is a genuine, pre-existing test-isolation bug independent of anything in this tranche — not introduced by the seal or replay, but newly surfaced by it.
positive_witness_results.verdict: PARTIAL_ALIVE — the tranche's own changes (nowhere near cache.rs) are not implicated; the underlying cargo test suite has a real, separate flake this checkpoint did not claim to fix

conclusion: The seal is real and the replay caught genuine issues a same-session receipt could not: two pre-existing bugs (a flaky cache test, a stale lockfile) that were invisible until tested from a truly clean, independent checkout. Per the promotion law, only W4PM-GALL-003 fully qualifies for ALIVE from this replay — its result reproduced bit-for-bit with a valid negative falsifier. 001, 002, 004A, 005A, 000 remain PARTIAL_ALIVE: their core fixes and mechanisms reproduced, but each has an open item (a discovered flake, an unrelated install failure, or a deferred full re-run) that must be resolved or explicitly scoped-out before full promotion — consistent with the user's corrected standing, not a full clearance of it.
